the refusal over an obstructed state root, beside the loop-lock and stop-flag arms

summary: `flume status` over a state root present and not a directory exits 1 with a raw stack out of the baton's mkdir — the one exit its own spec says it never takes
acceptance: the baton construction is inside a guard that reports `EX_IOERR` naming the state root, the disposition `status`'s two later reads already take, so exit 1 stays unreachable and no observation prints as its opposite
tests: flume status refuses an obstructed state root with the io-error exit code rather than a raw stack
notes: Measured this tick over a scratch repo carrying a plain file at `.flume`: exit 1, `ENOTDIR ... mkdir '<root>/.flume/awake'` out of `src/Baton.ts:63` via `src/cli.ts:324`, ahead of the guards at `:355` and `:427`. `src/cli.ts:360` names exit 1 as the one exit `status` is specced never to take. The mkdir itself stays: the cited section declares it status's one filesystem effect. Drained from note THE-ENGINES-REMAINING-ABSENT-ARMS-PROVE-THEIR-ANCESTRY, item 1.
